findings: Twelve-month real return, judged out of sample from 1940 with purged walk-forward refits: the ensemble's skill against the historical mean is +4.0% (Diebold-Mariano t 1.6); the best single model is combination of one-variable forecasts, restricted at +2.5%. Across 28 combinatorial purged splits the chance that picking the in-sample winner misleads is 82%.

Since v0.25 the ensemble truncates each member's forecast at zero and shrinks the average toward the historical mean with a weight learned only from forecasts whose outcome was known (today 0.00, average 0.46); the equal-weight v0.24 ensemble scored -6.0%. The crash ensemble is shrunk toward the base rate the same way (Brier skill -2.8% against -11.6%). Each was chosen from the variants tried (11 for returns, 7 for crashes), so the margins are smaller than their t statistics suggest.
Today the ensemble expects +6.6% real over the next year against a historical +6.6%, with an 80% conformal interval of plus or minus 20% in log terms (past intervals covered 82%).
A fall of 15% or more within a year: the ensemble puts it at 21% against a base rate of 21%; its Brier skill out of sample is -2.8% and AUC 0.52.
Is today familiar? Its 24 nearest historical months are further away than they are for 25% of months in the record.
